title: Fraction Frontier
goal: I can change between improper fractions and mixed numbers. I can find a fraction of a set and compare fractions with different denominators.

learn.intro: A fraction bar shows equal parts of one whole. A fraction of a set uses a bar model: divide the total by the denominator to find 1 unit.

steps: 5 fifths make 1 whole. Divide: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 with 2 left.

example2.problem: There are 48 stickers. 5/6 of them are gold. How many are gold?

howto.title: How to do it
steps: Improper to mixed: divide the top by the bottom.
Mixed to improper: whole × bottom + top, over the bottom.
Fraction of a set: 1 unit is the total ÷ the bottom number.

facts.title: Comparing
lines: Same bottom: the greater top is more.
Same top: the smaller bottom is more.
Equivalent: multiply or divide top and bottom by the same number.
Whole from a part: 3 units = 36, so 1 unit = 12.

try.explanation: 3 wholes are 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. 15 fifths and 4 more fifths make 19 fifths: 19/5.

items.text: Each bar is 1 whole cut into sixths. Look at the shaded parts.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many sixths are shaded? {b} sixths

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write it as a mixed number. {b} {b}/{b}

items.explanation: There are 6 + 6 + 5 = 17 sixths shaded. 2 whole bars are shaded and 5 of the 6 parts of the third bar: 2 5/6.

items.text: Write each as a mixed number.
items.explanation: (a) 19 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 3. (b) 23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5. (c) 31 ÷ 8 = 3 remainder 7. (d) 40 ÷ 5 = 8 with nothing left, so it is exactly 8.

items.text: Write each as an improper fraction.
items.explanation: (a) 3 × 5 + 2 = 17 fifths. (b) 5 × 3 + 1 = 16 thirds. (c) 2 × 8 + 7 = 23 eighths.

items.text: A box has 36 pencils. 5/9 of them are red.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many pencils are red? {b} pencils

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many are not red? {b} pencils

items.explanation: 9 units = 36, so 1 unit = 36 ÷ 9 = 4. Red is 5 units: 5 × 4 = 20 pencils. Not red is 4 units: 4 × 4 = 16 pencils.

items.text: The number line is marked in thirds. Write the number each arrow shows.
items.explanation: Each step is 1/3. A is 2 steps from 0: 2/3. B is 1 whole and 1 more step: 1 1/3. C is 8 steps from 0, so 8/3, which is 2 2/3.

items.text: Mei has read 3/7 of her book. She has read 36 pages.

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many pages are left to read? {b} pages

items.explanation: 3 units = 36 pages, so 1 unit = 12 pages. The whole book is 7 units: 7 × 12 = 84 pages. Left is 4 units: 4 × 12 = 48 pages.

items.text: Circle the correct sign.
items.explanation: (a) 3/4 = 6/8, and 6/8 is more than 5/8. (b) 4/6 = 8/12, and 8/12 is more than 7/12. (c) 3/8 is less than 1/2 and 5/9 is more than 1/2. (d) Both have 5 parts, and sixths are larger than eighths.

items.text: Fill in the missing numbers.
Each pizza is cut into 8 slices. The children eat 27 slices.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many pizzas is that? {b} {b}/{b} pizzas

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many slices are in 5 whole pizzas? {b} slices

parts.label: c
parts.text: How many more slices make 4 whole pizzas? {b} slices

items.explanation: (a) 27 ÷ 8 = 3 remainder 3, so 3 3/8 pizzas. (b) 5 × 8 = 40. (c) 4 pizzas are 32 slices, and 32 − 27 = 5.

items.text: A jug holds 2 1/2 litres of juice. Each cup holds 1/4 litre.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many cups can a full jug fill? {b} cups

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ravi fills 6 cups. How much juice is left? {b} litre

items.explanation: Each litre has 4 quarters. 2 1/2 litres is 10 quarters, so 10 cups. After 6 cups, 4 quarters are left, and 4 quarters make 1 litre.

items.text: Aisha has 48 stickers. Mei gets 1/4 of the stickers. Ben gets 1/3 of the stickers that are left. How many stickers does Aisha keep? {b}
items.explanation: 1/4 of 48 is 12, so she has 48 − 12 = 36 left. 1/3 of 36 is 12. Then 36 − 12 = 24 stickers.

items.text: How many?
items.explanation: (a) 5 × 4 = 20. (b) 3 × 6 = 18. (c) 2 wholes make 4 halves, and 1/2 makes 1 more half: 5 halves.

items.text:
n is a whole number. It makes 1/2 < n/9 < 5/6 true. Find the least and the greatest value of n.
Least {b}   Greatest {b}
items.hint: Make all 3 fractions have the same bottom number. Try 18.
items.explanation: Use 18 on the bottom: 1/2 = 9/18, n/9 = 2n/18 and 5/6 = 15/18. So 9 < 2n < 15 and n is 5, 6 or 7. The least is 5 and the greatest is 7.

items.text: In one day Ali sleeps 1/3 of the 24 hours and is at school for 1/4 of the 24 hours. He plays for half of the hours that are left. How many hours does he play? {b} hours
items.hint: How many hours are left after sleep and school?
items.explanation: 1/3 of 24 = 8 hours and 1/4 of 24 = 6 hours. 24 − 8 − 6 = 10 hours are left. Half of 10 is 5 hours.

items.text: In a class, 1/3 of the children are boys. 3/4 of the girls wear glasses. 18 girls wear glasses. How many children are in the class? {b}
items.hint: The girls are 2/3 of the class. Find 3/4 of 2/3.
items.explanation: The girls are 2/3 of the class. 3/4 of 2/3 is 6/12 = 1/2 of the class. 1/2 of the class is 18, so the class has 2 × 18 = 36 children.

items.text: Think about fractions with denominator 20 that are greater than 1/4 and less than 3/5.
items.hint: Write 1/4 and 3/5 as twentieths. List the ones in between.

items.text: Write each fraction as a sum of 2 different unit fractions. A unit fraction has 1 on top.
In a class, 2/5 of the children are girls. 1/3 of the girls wear glasses. 6 girls wear glasses. How many children are in the class? {b}
items.hint: Find the number of girls first.
items.explanation: 6 girls are 1/3 of the girls, so there are 18 girls. 18 girls are 2/5 of the class, so 1/5 is 9 children and the class has 5 × 9 = 45 children.

items.text: Compare each pair. Circle the correct sign.
items.hint: How far is each fraction from 1?
items.explanation: (a) 7/9 is 2/9 short of 1 and 8/10 is 2/10 short of 1. 2/9 is more than 2/10, so 7/9 is less. (b) 1/12 is less than 1/10, so 11/12 is greater. (c) 1/15 is more than 1/20, so 14/15 is less.

items.text: Write 29/6 as a mixed number. {b} {b}/{b}
items.explanation: 29 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 5. That is 4 wholes and 5 sixths: 4 5/6.

items.text: Write 5 3/8 as an improper fraction. {b}/{b}
Which is greater, 5/8 or 7/12? Circle it. {circ:5/8|7/12}
items.explanation: In twenty-fourths, 5/8 = 15/24 and 7/12 = 14/24. 15/24 is greater, so 5/8 is greater.

items.text: 4/9 of the beads in a bag are blue. There are 28 blue beads. How many beads are in the bag? {b}
items.explanation: 4 units = 28, so 1 unit = 7. The bag is 9 units: 9 × 7 = 63 beads.
